newsitem.title: USA: Eastern U.S. seen hit by Artic blast next week.
newsitem.headline: Eastern U.S. seen hit by Artic blast next week.

text.p: The eastern United States could be hit by an Artic blast next week, with freezing temperatures possibly as far south as Florida, meteorologists said.

"It is going to whack the eastern half (of the U.S.), from the eastern Plains to eastern Seaboard, next Tuesday and Wednesday. Temperatures will be much below normal," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc.
"The freeze line would get as far south as Tampa/Orlando, Florida," he added, noting the cold snap could endanger crops in key citrus growing areas.
Gesser said lows in the upper Midwest would be around zero Fahrenheit, single digits in the lower Midwest and 10s to 20s F along the east coast.
Mike Palmerino, senior agricultural meteorologist for Weather Services Corp, also said there was potential for sharply lower temperatures early next week.
He said it was difficult at this stage to be precise about how low temperatures could get and saw the cold snap hitting the Plains and Midwest around next Tuesday.
This week's conditions are mostly mild although hog movement could be disrupted early this week, meteorologists said.
Palmerino said there may be some problems transporting hogs in Nebraska, south Dakota and Iowa with around three to six inches of snow expected Monday/early Tuesday.
Gesser estimated snowfall in that area from four to six inches with southern Minnesota, Wisconsin and the extreme northwest of Illinois also likely to be hit.

He said winds of 25 to 30 mph were developing behind the snow system, which could further disrupt hog movement. Temperatures, however, will be only slightly below normal with lows in the teens to low 20s.
The northeast should, however, be mild this week.

Palmerino said temperatures in the north-east would be up to 10 degrees above normal in the first half of the week, cooling off a bit to two to four degress above normal Thursday and then dipping to slightly below normal Friday/Saturday.
